ce_bugs.text: Webhook secret header lookup is case-sensitive on the header name while Node lowercases incoming headers, and comparison is not constant-time

.env.example documents a 32-byte encryption key but suggests openssl rand -base64 24 which produces only 24 bytes
Webhook credential sync endpoint authenticates only with static shared secret, no per-user authorization, allowing credential overwrite for any user/app

Salesforce uses unreliable response.statusText !== 'OK' success check
Node headers for repeated header names are arrays, which will never equal the string secret, causing false 403s

mrv_findings.text: googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts persists the Zod SafeParseReturnType wrapper as the credential key instead of the token payload, breaking all subsequent Google Calendar API calls
parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts uses [z.string().toString()] which evaluates to the literal string "[object Object]", making the schema's numeric expiry matching dead code and keys overwrite each other

parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts unconditionally injects a fake refresh_token "refresh_token", which callers spread into persisted credentials and overwrite real refresh tokens; also accessing .refresh_token on the safeParse result is a TS error
refreshOAuthTokens.ts returns a fetch Response in sync mode, but zoho-bigin and zohocrm CalendarService callers treat it as an axios response reading .data, causing errors/undefined branches
hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts uses the fetch Response from refreshOAuthTokens as a HubspotToken, so fields like refresh_token are undefined when sync mode is enabled

googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts sync branch returns a fetch Response (or GaxiosResponse in fallback) but the caller reads res?.data, which only exists on the Gaxios shape, persisting undefined access_token/expiry_date

salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts performs an unconditional network token refresh on every service instantiation with no feature flag or try/catch, and checks unreliable response.statusText !== "OK" instead of response.ok, potentially rejecting valid credentials
APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED in packages/lib/constants.ts is a raw env string rather than a boolean, causing type defects and surprising behavior for consumers treating it as a boolean flag

Rename of encodeOAuthState/decodeOAuthState/createOAuthAppCredential in _utils/oauth may leave untouched importers (e.g. apps/api routes) with broken module paths; verify with a repo-wide grep before merge
No delete/revoke path in the credential sync webhook protocol; synced Credential rows live forever after upstream disconnect
Webhook endpoint has no HTTP method guard (GET/PUT/DELETE hit same handler) and unhandled zod/JSON.parse/symmetricDecrypt failures return 500 with stack trace on an unauthenticated endpoint
symmetricDecrypt proceeds with an empty string when CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY is unset
.env.example is self-contradictory: says key must be 32 bytes but instructs `openssl rand -base64 24`; no startup validation of key length
No tests for new behavior: webhook endpoint, refreshOAuthTokens, parseRefreshTokenResponse have zero coverage and no E2E distinguishing APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED true/false

parseRefreshTokenResponse result stored whole without .success check in googlecalendar CalendarService.ts:96, persisting {success:false, error} as credential key and corrupting it; zoomvideo has same unchecked shape

Zod index signatures in parseRefreshTokenResponse don't work as catch-all, causing fields to be stripped and fake refresh_token injected in sync mode; no defined response contract for CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT

Salesforce CalendarService.ts:75-98 unconditionally fetches refresh tokens not gated by APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and doesn't check credentialKey.refresh_token exists, causing 400 for legacy credentials

refreshOAuthTokens.ts has no error handling, timeout, or response-status check on sync fetch, no fallback to local refreshFunction, and downstream services still parse responses as provider-native shapes, so expiryDate computations are wrong with sync tokens
No validation or startup check for new env vars; CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT set without encryption key yields a half-enabled configuration
apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts auth check compares header against env var with no null/timing handling

Credential-injection webhook ships unconditionally in core webapp (only soft-gated by APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED), not traceable to PR requirements; exposing a write-to-Credential-DB endpoint for any deployment that sets the env vars

Salesforce CalendarService adds unconditional token-refresh fetch on every service construction, not gated by APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED or refreshOAuthTokens — extra round-trip + prisma write with no feature-flag control
Salesforce token refresh bypasses CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT, so Salesforce never syncs even when credential sharing is enabled
zoho-bigin add.ts switches redirectUri from appConfig.slug interpolation to a hardcoded string, risking silent divergence from callback route if the app slug changes

parseRefreshTokenResponse uses minimumTokenResponseSchema with dynamic keys expanding to literal 'undefined', validating nothing and stripping fields — stored credential key loses refresh_token and other provider fields when sharing is enabled

APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED uses truthy-string semantics (e.g. '0' or 'false' are truthy) diverging from the repo's ENV === '1' boolean pattern, risking accidental enablement of the credential-write webhook

parseRefreshTokenResponse() returns the safeParse result object but the Google call site uses it as parsed data, persisting {success, data} wrapper into Credential.key and breaking Google Calendar after token refresh

Zod schema uses computed keys [z.string().toString()] as a wildcard-key attempt, which produces a garbage literal; schema doesn't validate expiry fields as intended, causing sync-mode responses to fail validation

Sync path POSTs to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT with no auth header, no timeout, no status check; the webhook handler rejects requests without the secret header, causing 403 responses parsed as token bodies
Downstream consumers (hubspot, zoho-bigin/zohocrm) expect different token response shapes but receive a raw fetch Response, reading undefined fields and silently succeeding with garbage credentials

APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is a truthy string expression instead of a boolean like other feature flags, inviting type drift
